payload.root_cause: In `slugify` (src/text.js:11), the call `.replace(/[\s-]+/, '-')` is missing the global regex flag `g`. String.prototype.replace with a non-global regex replaces only the first match, so only the first whitespace run becomes a dash while subsequent runs are left as-is. For input 'Hello Big  World!': after lowercasing, trimming, and stripping '!' (line 10), we get 'hello big  world'; line 11 converts only the first space, producing 'hello-big  world'; the final edge-dash trim (line 12) changes nothing, yielding the observed 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. The fix is to add the `g` flag: `.replace(/[\s-]+/g, '-')`.

With a non-global regex, `String.prototype.replace` substitutes only the first `[\s-]+` run, so 'hello big  world' became 'hello-big  world' instead of 'hello-big-world'. Adding the `g` flag makes every whitespace/dash run collapse into a single dash, fixing both test cases ('Hello Big  World!' and '  Already-slugged  title '). No other behavior changes: the surrounding lines (strip and edge-dash trim) already use `g` and are correct.
